text:
jamal: Heads up — around 10:12 we saw a big backlog for gpu inference pods in us-west1, dozens Pending, autoscaler didn't kick the on-demand fallback pool. Wondering if CA ignored the group due to label mismatch.

infra-bot: [alert] spot-interruption notice received for nodepool=spot-gpu-west-1 (GCP preemptions). Affected nodes: 12, start draining.

alex: I see CA logs showing scale-up was considered but then skipped: `scaleUp skipped for NodeGroup dedicated-on-demand: node group tainted=no-fallback:NoSchedule` — looks like we accidentally added a taint to the on-demand group in the last config update. :facepalm:

jamal: ahhh. That matches: evicted spot nodes + tainted fallback = nowhere to land pods. Can someone paste `kubectl get pods -A` snippet?

tina: quick output:
```
NAMESPACE     NAME                                READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
vision-ns     vision-infer-xyz-0                  0/1     Pending   0          3m
vision-ns     vision-infer-xyz-1                  0/1     Pending   0          3m
batch-ns      batch-train-2026-03-18-0           0/1     Pending   0          6m
```
reason: Pods show `0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taint {no-fallback:NoSchedule}` or `Insufficient gpu`.

priya: Also noticed SNAT IP exhaustion alerts when cluster scaled up previously — scaling 40 nodes in <2m exhausts NAT IPs on our NAT gateway and kubelets fail to join. That could be compounding the issue (nodes not Ready).

alex: Good call. Two separate but related failures: (1) fallback group tainted so CA refused to place, (2) rapid scale-up bumped into VPC NAT/snatte limits so new nodes stuck in NotReady.

sre-lead: Quick mitigation: remove the taint from the on-demand fallback group and set a short rolling window so CA will consider it. I'll push a hotfix to remove `no-fallback:NoSchedule` from nodepool config. After that we should see CA proceed.

jamal: For medium-term: propose we maintain a small warm pool of 4 on-demand GPUs with `taint=prefer-fallback:NoExecute` (soft), and add an alert for >5 unschedulable pods with reason matching `taint` vs `Insufficient` so we can differentiate. Also add a pre-warm policy for NAT IPs (allocate extra external IPs on burst).

priya: Agreed. Also let's add a CA annotation/label check to our CI so changes that add taints to fallback pools fail pre-merge. I can make a Linters PR.

alex: config snippet I'll apply now to remove the taint:
```
# Patch nodepool
gcloud container node-pools update dedicated-on-demand \
  --cluster=prod-us-west1 \
  --remove-taints=no-fallback:NoSchedule
```

jamal: thanks. Once off, monitor PodPending and NAT metrics. If NAT issue persists we should throttle scale-up rate: add a max Surge or cooldown to CA.

infra-bot: [info] scale action executed: removed taint from nodepool dedicated-on-demand by alex at 10:20.

tina: pods are scheduling now, backlog draining. Still watching NAT IPs while we roll the standby nodes back up slowly.

sre-lead: Follow-ups: (1) warm-pool PR (2) NAT autoscaling/capacity plan (3) pre-merge lint preventing taints on fallback pools. Assigning to priya/alex/jamal. :white_check_mark:

priya: I'll open the lint PR and add tests for labels by EOD.

jamal: I'll write the runbook step to check `kubectl describe nodes` + NAT metrics for next time. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
